default.py:215-242 builds records via json.dumps: text records {kind:'text',content}, pair records {kind:'sql_example',question,sql}; output is _CONTEXT_PREFIX + JSON array + _CONTEXT_SUFFIX (lines 34,36 give <sqllens_memory_data>...</sqllens_memory_data>), with <,>,& escaped so splitting on delimiters is safe. tests/unit/test_enhancer_context_band.py:161-162 parses it by splitting on the delimiters then json.loads. Nuance: each record carries only the keys relevant to its kind, not all four; the optional omitted note follows the closing delimiter.

default.py:233-234 replaces <,>,& in json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) output. In JSON text these characters can only occur inside string values, never inside an escape sequence (escapes are \\, \", \n, \uXXXX with hex digits only). An escaped backslash followed by '<' becomes \\\u003c, which parses as backslash then '<'. \u003c etc. are valid JSON escapes decoding to the originals, so the document stays valid and round-trips. Test at test_memory_context_boundary.py:53-63 asserts decoded content/question/sql equal originals containing < > & and quotes.

default.py:226-242: remaining = 32768 - len(prefix) - len(suffix) - len(omitted) - 2 is reserved up front, always including the omission notice. Each record's cost (len + comma separator) is deducted and skipped if it exceeds remaining. The output is prefix + '[' + joined + ']' + suffix + optional omitted, so its length is at most prefix + 2 + (sum of costs <= remaining) + suffix + omitted <= 32768 in all branches. The prefix, suffix and notice constants (lines 27-37) are small, so remaining starts positive. The escaping replaces happen before len() is taken, so the cost is exact.

default.py:233-234 json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=True) then replaces every '<', '>' and '&' with \u003c/\u003e/\u0026. Record keys/kinds are fixed literals, so any '<' in the output comes from stored values and is escaped; the only raw '<' between prefix and suffix is none. Pre-escaped input: a stored literal backslash-u003c has its backslash doubled by json.dumps (becomes \\u003c), so it stays inert text and cannot yield a raw '<'. Hence '</sqllens_memory_data>' cannot be emitted inside the block (delimiters at lines 34/36 are added only by the code). Bounding via _cap and _CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS budget (lines 226-240). Claim covers delimiters only; line 214 explicitly disclaims injection guarantee.

default.py:233-234: json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) escapes newlines/control chars as \n, \uXXXX; then <, >, & are replaced with \u003c/\u003e/\u0026, so the encoded record contains no raw angle brackets. Adversarial traces: content with literal text \u003c is dumped as \\u003c (escaped backslash), no '<' to replace, decodes back to the literal text, cannot forge a delimiter; content '\<' becomes \\ + \u003c, which is still correct JSON. Raw '</tag>' becomes \u003c/tag\u003e. Only the fixed _CONTEXT_PREFIX/SUFFIX contain real delimiters (line 241).

default.py:208-209 _cap truncates to limit including marker. Lines 20,21,25 set 4000/1000/8000 and 216-223 apply them (SQL gets a '-- (SQL truncated)' marker). Line 233-234 json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) escapes newlines and control chars, and < > & are replaced with \u003c/\u003e/\u0026, so stored text cannot close </sqllens_memory_data>. Lines 226-240 reserve prefix, suffix, omitted note and brackets from 32768 and skip records that exceed the remainder, so the total stays at or below 32768. Hostile input: a content with '</sqllens_memory_data>' is escaped in the output. A very large record is skipped.
